why: The student gets the right value (-2147483648) and explains it by applying the int range rule to this one case: +2147483648 is outside the int range, so the result cannot become positive. They don't go on to explain how the value wraps back or relate it to anything else in the code, so it stays at L2.

concepts.quote: Still -2147483648, because +2147483648 does not fit in an int.
concepts.why: The answer applies the 32-bit range rule to this specific result and correctly concludes that the out-of-range value stays at -2147483648.
The answer makes no claim about primitive types in general.
The answer is about a value computed at run time, not about the limits on int literals.
The answer does not mention long.
